text: Name every organisation that appears on the project with grant agreement number 101036871, giving for each one the role it is recorded under.
gold_sql: SELECT name, role FROM organization WHERE projectID = 101036871
reference_answer: All thirteen organisations recorded on grant agreement 101036871 hold the same role, thirdParty: HUB ONE, BUREAU VERITAS ITALIA SPA, INEO ENERGY AND SYSTEMS, THE MANCHESTER METROPOLITAN UNIVERSITY, RINA TECH UK LTD, DEUTSCHES ZENTRUM FUR LUFT - UND RAUMFAHRT EV, MZLZ-ZEMALJSKE USLUGE DOO, ENGIE GLOBAL MARKETS, ENGIE ENERGIE SERVICES, ECOLE NATIONALE SUPERIEURE DES MINES DE PARIS, UNIVERSITA DEGLI STUDI DI MODENA E REGGIO EMILIA, L AIR LIQUIDE SA and ATTRIBUTES. Not one of them is entered as coordinator or as participant.
notes: Grounded on corpus-profile seed sql-09 (the coordinator-role invariant). Executed this pass: the gold SQL returns 13 rows, every one role='thirdParty' (row_count 13, not truncated). Context re-executed as a drift check, not part of the gold: 'SELECT p.id FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id GROUP BY p.id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.role='coordinator' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)=0' -> exactly one row, 101036871; the >1-coordinator counterpart returns 0. So this project is the corpus's single coordinator-less grant, and its organisation table holds only thirdParty rows. Project row: acronym OLGA, title 'Holistic & Green Airports', status SIGNED, IA, 2021-10-01..2026-09-30, ecMaxContribution 24,991,644.02, while every one of the 13 organisation rows carries ecContribution 0.00 (the sf-04 project-vs-organisation money divergence). No schema_docs value note is needed to write the gold SQL - the filter is a literal primary-key id on one table - so the entry is lookup, not value-grounded. sql_comparison=set: the answer is a set of (organisation, role) pairs, order carries no meaning. Wording note (fix round): the question demands the enumeration explicitly ('name every organisation ... giving for each one the role') because all 13 rows share one role value, so a role-only answer would otherwise be defensible while scoring short against the pinned name+role payload.

text: Across the Horizon 2020 projects that were terminated, what was the average overall project budget, counting all funding sources and not only the EU contribution?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(totalCost) AS avg_total_cost FROM project WHERE status = 'TERMINATED'
reference_answer: The 2,127 Horizon 2020 projects carrying the terminated status had an average overall budget of about 726,697.97 EUR (executed mean 726697.974029149). That is the full project cost across all funding sources, so it sits well above the average EU contribution of those same projects.
notes: Grounded 2026-07-29 on project.status (three values, executed corpus-wide: CLOSED 30,298 / SIGNED 2,964 / TERMINATED 2,127). Gold measures project.totalCost, which schema_docs sd2 defines as EU funding plus participants' own resources and explicitly not 'EU funding'. Distribution over the 2,127 terminated rows: 0 NULLs, 3 zeros, min 0.00, max 117,894,748.75. Discriminator (not a trap subtype, no wrong query recorded as gold-adjacent): a system that reads 'budget' as the EU contribution returns AVG(ecMaxContribution) = 555712.0245745181, a clearly different number from the gold 726697.974029149. Single table, single non-trivial WHERE, no GROUP BY, no ordering -> L1 aggregate.

text: Across all ERC Advanced Grant projects, how much EU money in total went to the organisations based in Switzerland?
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.ecContribution), 2) AS ec_contribution_eur FROM organization o JOIN project p ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE o.country = 'CH' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-ADG'
reference_answer: Adding up what each Switzerland-based participant was allocated across the ERC Advanced Grant (ERC-ADG) projects it took part in gives an EU contribution of 340205306.48 EUR.
notes: Executed 2026-07-29. The join is load-bearing in both directions: the funding scheme (ERC-ADG) lives only on project, the country and the per-organisation money only on organization, so neither table answers this alone. Grain and column both have to be right: SUM(o.ecContribution) over the join = 340205306.48; summing project.ecMaxContribution over the same join rows (the sf-03 inflation error) = 375878753.04; summing ecMaxContribution once per distinct ERC-ADG project with a Swiss participant = 361587397.04. All 151 Swiss participation rows in ERC-ADG projects have a non-null ecContribution (2 are explicitly 0.00), spanning 145 distinct projects, so no NULL handling is needed; netEcContribution is identical here (340205306.48), so 'net' vs gross is not a second reading. fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC%' has 7 values (ERC-STG 2771, ERC-COG 2254, ERC-ADG 1584, ERC-POC 967, ERC-POC-LS 158, ERC-SyG 99, ERC-LVG 5); only ERC-ADG is the Advanced Grant.
